title: Sort List
statement_short: Given the head of a linked list, return the list after sorting it in ascending order. Write an algorithm that runs in O(n log n) time and O(1) auxiliary memory.
constraints: 0 <= number of nodes in list <= 5 \* 10^4, -10^5 <= Node.val <= 10^5
hint: Node count up to 5 \* 10^4 and O(n log n) time mandate divide-and-conquer merge sort using fast/slow pointers for middle splitting.
why_not: Right: Linked List (Fast & Slow) finds list midpoints to split lists for merge sort in O(n log n) time and O(log n) stack space (or O(1) bottom-up). Not Sorting: Standard array sorting algorithms require transferring nodes into an array with O(n) extra space. Not Two Pointers: Opposite-end pointer swaps require doubly linked lists or random indexing unavailable in singly linked lists. Not Heap / Priority Queue: Storing nodes in a min-heap takes O(n) auxiliary space.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(log n) space
